classification.difficultyReason: Consider multiple possible transversals and identify missing, unique or multiple interior-pair answers.

inlines.text: Label the missing angle arc for the corresponding, alternate, or co-interior angle.
There can be more than one answer, or no answer.

spec.description: Two unmarked crossed lines and a steep ascending transversal; upper given arc in the left sector. No printed vertex labels.
spec.mathematics: T and V are coordinate-only intersections. Given sector A–T–E. No parallelism asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Black given arc only; supplied blue response omitted.

answer.short: Mark the lower-left angle at the lower intersection.
answer.worked: The corresponding angle is below the lower line and left of the transversal, matching the given angle's position.

spec.description: One corresponding response arc at the lower intersection.

spec.description: Upper gently descending line, lower horizontal line and steep ascending transversal.
spec.mathematics: Given upper left sector A–T–E; no parallel marks.

answer.short: Mark the upper-right angle at the lower intersection.
answer.worked: The alternate angle is inside the two lines and on the opposite side of the transversal.

spec.description: Upper-right response arc at the lower intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector D–V–F.

spec.description: Upper descending line, lower horizontal line and ascending transversal, with plain endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Given upper left sector A–T–E; no parallelism asserted.

answer.short: Mark the upper-left angle at the lower intersection.
answer.worked: The co-interior angle is inside the two lines and on the same side of the transversal.

spec.description: Upper-left response arc at the lower intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector F–V–C.

spec.description: Two shallow ascending parallel lines crossed by a steep descending transversal.
spec.mathematics: Matching single right-pointing chevrons; given upper right sector E–T–B.
spec.answerVisibility: Black given arc and parallel marks only.

answer.short: Mark the right-hand angle below the lower parallel line.
answer.worked: At the lower intersection, match the given angle's position below the parallel line and right of the transversal.

spec.description: Right-hand lower-intersection response arc.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector E–V–D.

spec.description: Two shallow ascending lines with matching chevrons and a descending transversal.
spec.mathematics: Given upper right sector E–T–B.
spec.answerVisibility: Black given arc and parallel marks only.

answer.short: Mark the angle above the lower line and left of the transversal.
answer.worked: Choose the interior angle at the lower intersection on the opposite side of the transversal.

spec.description: Left-hand interior response arc at the lower intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector F–V–C.

spec.description: Ascending parallel pair crossed by a steep descending transversal.
spec.mathematics: Single matching right-pointing chevrons; upper right given sector E–T–B.

answer.short: Mark the upper sector at the lower intersection.
answer.worked: Choose the interior angle above the lower parallel line on the same side of the transversal as the given angle.

spec.description: Upper interior response arc at the lower intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector D–V–F.

spec.description: Two steep ascending parallel lines crossed by a shallow ascending transversal.
spec.mathematics: Downward chevrons below the transversal. Given sector E–R–C.

answer.short: Mark the lower-left sector at the left intersection.
answer.worked: Match the given position below the transversal and left of the steep line.

spec.description: Lower-left response arc at the left intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector E–L–A.

spec.description: Steep ascending parallel pair and shallow ascending transversal.
spec.mathematics: Matching downward chevrons; given right-intersection sector E–R–C.

answer.short: Mark the angle above the transversal and right of the left steep line.
answer.worked: The alternate angle lies between the steep lines, on the opposite side of the transversal.

spec.description: Upper-right interior response arc at the left intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector F–L–B.

spec.description: Two steep ascending lines with matching downward chevrons and a shallow transversal.
spec.mathematics: Given right-intersection lower-left sector E–R–C.

answer.short: Mark the angle below the transversal and right of the left steep line.
answer.worked: The co-interior angle lies between the steep lines and below the transversal, on the same side as the given angle.

spec.description: Lower-right interior response arc at the left intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor sector A–L–F.

spec.description: Two descending oblique strokes with upper-left arrow-shaped marks and a nearly vertical transversal.
spec.mathematics: Given obtuse exterior sector B–T–F. Terminal mark semantics unresolved; geometry preserves appearance.
spec.answerVisibility: Black given arc and source terminal marks only.

answer.short: Mark the right-hand obtuse sector at the lower intersection.
answer.worked: Match the sector between the upward transversal arm and the down-right oblique arm at the lower intersection.

spec.description: Right-hand obtuse response arc at the lower intersection.
spec.mathematics: Minor obtuse sector D–V–F.

spec.description: Descending oblique pair with upper-left terminal arrow-shaped marks and nearly vertical transversal.
spec.mathematics: Given upper exterior obtuse sector B–T–F. Alternate means alternate interior in the teaching context.

answer.worked: The given angle is exterior. Alternate pairs in this booklet must both be inside the two lines.

spec.description: Descending oblique strokes with upper-left arrow-shaped terminal marks and a nearly vertical transversal.
spec.mathematics: Given upper exterior obtuse sector B–T–F.

answer.worked: The given angle is exterior, so it cannot form a co-interior pair.

spec.description: Four extended unmarked lines; steep ascending sides, ascending top and descending bottom.
spec.mathematics: Given upper-left sector C–BR–H. Either the bottom or right line can be the transversal. No parallelism asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Black given arc only; both supplied blue arcs omitted.

answer.short: Mark two arcs: upper-left at the bottom-left and top-right intersections.
answer.worked: Using the bottom line as transversal gives the upper-left angle at the bottom-left intersection. Using the right line as transversal gives the angle above the top line and left of the right line.

spec.description: Both corresponding response arcs.
spec.mathematics: Minor sectors F–BL–C and H–TR–A.

spec.description: Four extended unmarked lines forming four intersections.
spec.mathematics: Given upper-left sector at BR; bottom and right lines give two possible transversals.

answer.short: Mark two arcs: lower-right at the bottom-left and top-right intersections.
answer.worked: Use the bottom and right lines separately as transversals. At each other intersection, mark the interior angle on the opposite side of that transversal.

spec.description: Both alternate interior response arcs.
spec.mathematics: Minor sectors E–BL–D and G–TR–B.

spec.description: Steep ascending side lines crossed by shallow ascending top and descending bottom lines.
spec.mathematics: Given upper-left sector at BR. Eight plain endpoints; no parallel marks.

answer.short: Mark the upper-right interior angle at the bottom-left intersection and the lower-left interior angle at the top-right intersection.
answer.worked: Use the bottom line as transversal to find the interior angle above it at the left intersection. Use the right line as transversal to find the interior angle left of it at the top intersection.

spec.description: Both co-interior response arcs.
spec.mathematics: Minor sectors D–BL–F and A–TR–G.

spec.description: Vertical left line and right line leaning right downward, crossed by two shallow ascending lines.
spec.mathematics: Given exterior lower-right sector G–BR–D; no parallelism asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Black given arc only; both blue response arcs omitted.

answer.short: Mark two arcs: lower-right at the bottom-left and top-right intersections.
answer.worked: Using the bottom line as transversal gives the lower-right angle at the left intersection. Using the right line as transversal gives the lower-right angle at the top intersection.

spec.description: Both corresponding response arcs.
spec.mathematics: Minor sectors E–BL–D and G–TR–B.

spec.description: Four unmarked extended lines with exterior lower-right given arc.
spec.mathematics: Given G–BR–D is exterior for both available transversal choices. Alternate pairs are interior only.

answer.worked: For either choice of transversal, the given angle is exterior. It cannot form an alternate interior pair.

spec.description: Vertical left and near-vertical right lines crossed by two gently ascending lines; plain endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Given lower-right sector G–BR–D is exterior for either available transversal.

answer.worked: For either choice of transversal, the given angle is exterior. Co-interior pairs require two interior angles.
